$comment: 🧠️ The graph memo: the slice a graph planner child produced once, kept beside the change journal and served again to the next identical request while the journal proves that nothing the planned generation read has changed. `relevance` is the closed table of what a fact row reads: `path` rows read the entry they name, `none` rows read nothing of the tree, `link` rows follow symbolic links, `resolve` rows resolve a request, `text` rows name their inputs inside their key. A kind this table does not name makes a generation unsealable (fail closed); a law keeps the table equal to the kinds the observation and generation schemas declare. Stamp refinement: the discovery frontier of a generation holds, per directory, the entry stamp (mtime, inode) captured with it; the planner itself treats a directory with an unmoved stamp (and not touched within the racy window of the capture) as one whose names, node types and absences cannot have moved (`stableDirectoriesV1`). A directory of the frontier whose facts are only entries and listings of kinds `Policy.stamped` is STAMPED: a row that adds, removes or renames a name directly inside it is relevant, a row that only says 'modified' (a content edit of a sibling no fact read; the kind is advisory) is settled by one lstat against the stamp kept in the table `.lst`. Directories a resolution or derived fact names, directories read by a kind of `Policy.following` (it follows symbolic links), and directories without a usable stamp are STRICT: every row directly inside is relevant (except the modification of a directory). `carry`: a sealed slice whose generation pointer moved is served under the newer generation when every generation-wide digest named in `shared` and the row of every owner the slice covers are identical in both manifests (the planner would verify the same facts and assemble the same projects from the same rows); otherwise the reason `pointer` names the first difference. Edit refinement: when the journal names a relevant change, the memo does not give up at once. The edit index of the sealed sidecar maps every entry to the rows that name it and every directory to the rows that read its children; the lookup re-checks exactly those rows with the planner's own checks (an analysis is replayed and compared by its result, so an edit that keeps a file's imports and modules holds), proves a directory that has relevant entries below it to be the same directory (frontier inode), lists a frontier directory whose children changed again with the planner's own walk predicates and compares its subdirectories and members, refuses a touched path that became a symbolic link, a row it cannot check (a derived fact, a closure) and more than `maximumEditPaths` paths or `maximumEditRows` rows; when everything holds it serves and re-seals the stamps of the directories it listed again. Derived refinement: a re-checked row that does not hold and that only pseudo owners hold (the support of derived facts), and a derived fact the journal names, make the memo ask those questions again with the planner's own derivation (`openGenerationDeriverV1`, `settleSuspectsV1`) in a child process of the same invocation (`Policy.derive`); it serves only when every answer is the recorded one and every new support reads only entries the old support read; a stale row a project or the environment holds itself, a failed or changed answer, a new entry and more than `maximumDerivedQuestions` questions plan. Outputs: a directory named in `Policy.outputs` is one a build writes its own results into (the git-ignored `.🧾️store`: temp file, lock directory, rename on every build). Its listing facts are not vouched for by the journal but re-checked by the engine on every lookup (they join the recheck set), and the directory is neither strict nor stamped; a row that names an entry or an ancestor is still relevant, a row directly inside is settled by the recorded listing. Assumption declared with the list: the graph takes no project, member or entry from such a directory.

warm.$comment: EN: The warm deriver (`🧮️derive/♨️warm`): a detached process of the run's exact implementation that answers derivation requests and keeps its TypeScript programs between them; its endpoint name prefix, how long it stays without a request, how long a run waits to connect and for an answer before it falls back to the derivation child, the largest request line, the resident size after which it stops after its answer (it keeps every program it built), and how often an idle deriver re-reads the size and modification time of every file of its captured closure and its own resident size: it stops at once when a file moved (its implementation was superseded, no run asks it any more) or it outgrew the resident size. DE: Der warme Ableiter (`🧮️derive/♨️warm`): ein abgelöster Prozess genau der Implementierung des Laufs, der Ableitungsanfragen beantwortet und seine TypeScript-Programme zwischen ihnen behält; das Präfix seines Endpunktnamens, wie lange er ohne Anfrage bleibt, wie lange ein Lauf auf die Verbindung und auf eine Antwort wartet, bevor er auf das Ableitungskind zurückfällt, die längste Anfragezeile die residente Größe, nach der er nach seiner Antwort aufhört (er behält jedes gebaute Programm), und wie oft ein untätiger Ableiter Größe und Änderungszeit jeder Datei seiner erfassten Hülle und seine eigene residente Größe neu liest: er hört sofort auf, wenn sich eine Datei bewegt hat (seine Implementierung wurde abgelöst, kein Lauf fragt ihn mehr) oder er über die residente Größe hinausgewachsen ist.

en.served: graph: {projects} projects served from the memo of {seconds} s ago; the journal vouches for {rows} facts and {rechecked} facts outside its sight held, no planner process was started
en.refused: graph: the memo cannot serve this request ({reason}); the graph is planned
en.carried: graph: the memo of generation {from} still describes generation {to}: the {projects} projects it serves are unchanged there
en.edited: graph: the memo re-checked the {rows} facts that read the {paths} changed paths with the planner's own checks; they all still hold
en.derived: graph: {questions} derived facts that read them were asked again by a child process with the planner's own derivation; every answer is unchanged

de.served: graph: {projects} Projekte aus dem Memo von vor {seconds} s geliefert; das Journal bürgt für {rows} Fakten, {rechecked} Fakten außerhalb seiner Sicht gelten noch, es wurde kein Planer-Prozess gestartet
de.refused: graph: das Memo kann diese Anfrage nicht bedienen ({reason}); der Graph wird geplant
de.carried: graph: das Memo der Generation {from} beschreibt auch Generation {to}: die {projects} gelieferten Projekte sind dort unverändert
de.edited: graph: das Memo hat die {rows} Fakten, welche die {paths} geänderten Pfade lesen, mit den Prüfungen des Planers nachgeprüft; alle gelten noch
de.derived: graph: {questions} abgeleitete Fakten, die sie lesen, wurden von einem Kindprozess mit der Ableitung des Planers neu befragt; jede Antwort ist unverändert

carried.$comment: The rows (positions in the fact index of `edit`) that an edit settlement found stale while every derived question they support answered the same: the memo served without a planner, so the sealed generation no longer describes these rows, and every later settlement re-checks them with the rows the journal names (a later change that restores one of their paths alone is then settled against the tree the questions were last asked on). Absent when there is nothing to carry; requires `edit`.

edit.$comment: The edit index of the sealed relevance (`id` = sha256 of the `.rix` file) and the fact index and frontier of the generation it was computed from: `index` names the rows by their position in that fact index, so a lookup fetches exactly the rows it re-checks from the immutable generation store; a retired index makes the memo plan.

state.$comment: light: the slice and the generation it served, kept after the first planner run; sealed: with the relevance of the generation, written by the run that found the same slice again, in the same generation or in a newer one whose rows of the slice are identical (Policy.carry), so the sealing cost is paid only by a repeated request, never by an edit-and-run loop.

Sidecar.$comment: The relevance of ONE served slice: `rows` counts the fact rows of the owners the served pin covers, of the environment owner and of the pseudo owners that support their derived facts (the selection the planner verified before it served the slice); a stale fact of an owner outside the slice never refuses it. A missing or foreign pin makes the sidecar unsealable (`pin`, `other-generation`). A slice the planner did not verify after the memo's journal cursor (served from a peer's verified stamp or from the pin of an outer invocation) is unsealable too (`unverified`): the sealing child is started with `requestedAt` set to the clock time right after the cursor, so a stamp serves it only when its observation began after the cursor, and the pin it records must not be older than that time.

edit.$comment: Written by the sealing child next to the relevance: `index` and `frontier` are the digests of the fact index and of the frontier of the served generation, `stem.rix` holds the edit index (the rows that name each entry, the rows that read the children of each directory, the directories with something relevant below them, the frontier directories and members).

DeriveRequest.$comment: Written by the memo for its derivation child (`Policy.derive` names the file): the fact index of the sealed generation and the pseudo owners whose derived question the child asks again.

DeriveAnswer.$comment: Written by the derivation child next to the request (`.answer.json`): `held` the questions whose answer is the recorded one and whose new support reads no entry the old support did not read, `changed` the questions whose answer moved, `failed` the computations that failed, `uncovered` the held questions whose new support reads a new entry (the memo's relevance does not watch it), `missing` when the fact index is no longer retained.

en.directory: The directory below the build store that holds the graph memo.
en.switch: The environment variable that switches the memo on or off (default on).
en.sidecar: The environment variable through which a planner child is told where to write its sealed slice.
en.derive: The environment variable that makes a child process answer a derivation request instead of planning.
en.warm: The warm deriver: the endpoint name prefix, the idle time, the connect and answer deadlines, the largest request line, the resident size limit and the closure check interval of the detached process that answers derivation requests.
en.recordSuffix: The suffix of a memo record.
en.planSuffix: The suffix of the planned slice kept beside a record.
en.relevanceSuffix: The suffix of the table of what each fact row reads.
en.recheckSuffix: The suffix of the facts the engine re-checks itself on every lookup.
en.stampSuffix: The suffix of the table of directory stamps.
en.editSuffix: The suffix of the edit index that maps every entry to the rows that name it.
en.maximumRecordBytes: The most bytes of a memo record that is read.
en.maximumPlanBytes: The most bytes of a planned slice that is read (256 MiB).
en.maximumRelevanceBytes: The most bytes of a relevance table that is read (64 MiB).
en.maximumRecheckBytes: The most bytes of a re-check table that is read (256 MiB).
en.maximumStampBytes: The most bytes of a stamp table that is read (64 MiB).
en.maximumEditBytes: The most bytes of an edit index that is read (128 MiB).
en.maximumEditPaths: The most changed paths an edit refinement re-checks before it plans instead.
en.maximumEditRows: The most rows an edit refinement re-checks before it plans instead.
en.maximumDerivedQuestions: The most derived facts the memo asks again in one child process.
en.maximumRows: The most fact rows a sealed slice may hold.
en.leafSymlinkCheckConcurrency: How many leaf paths are checked for symbolic links at once.
en.environmentPrefixes: The prefixes of the environment variables that are part of the memo key.
en.argumentsDenied: The arguments that are not part of the memo key.
en.stamped: The fact kinds whose directory listings are vouched for by directory stamps.
en.following: The fact kinds that follow symbolic links.
en.outputs: The directories a build writes its own results into; their listings are re-checked on every lookup.
en.environmentDenied: The environment variables that never belong to the memo key.
en.relevance: The closed table of what each fact kind reads.
en.carry: Which generation-wide digests must be identical for a sealed slice to be served under a newer generation.
en.texts: The English and German notices of the memo.
en.expect: The environment variable that carries the memo state a planner child is expected to find.
en.planOutput: The environment variable through which a planner child is told where to write the plan of the graph.
en.requestedAt: The environment variable that carries the instant the graph was requested.
en.pointerMaximumBytes: The most bytes of a generation pointer file that is read (64 KiB).
en.deriveMaximumNames: The most names a derivation request or answer lists.
en.deriveNameCharacters: The most characters of one name in a derivation request or answer.
en.abortCheckMask: The mask of the row counter: the row loop checks for cancellation whenever the counter under it is zero.
en.planFlushBytes: The size at which the plan writer flushes its buffer to the file (1 MiB).
en.planArrayChunkRows: The array elements the plan writer serializes at once.

de.directory: Das Verzeichnis unterhalb des Build-Speichers, das das Graph-Memo hält.
de.switch: Die Umgebungsvariable, die das Memo ein- oder ausschaltet (Standard ein).
de.sidecar: Die Umgebungsvariable, die einem Planer-Kind sagt, wohin es seinen versiegelten Ausschnitt schreibt.
de.derive: Die Umgebungsvariable, die ein Kindprozess dazu bringt, eine Ableitungsanfrage zu beantworten statt zu planen.
de.warm: Der warme Ableiter: das Präfix des Endpunktnamens, die Leerlaufzeit, die Verbindungs- und Antwortfristen, die längste Anfragezeile, die Grenze der residenten Größe und das Prüfintervall der Hülle des abgelösten Prozesses, der Ableitungsanfragen beantwortet.
de.planSuffix: Die Endung des geplanten Ausschnitts neben einem Eintrag.
de.relevanceSuffix: Die Endung der Tabelle dessen, was jede Faktenzeile liest.
de.recheckSuffix: Die Endung der Fakten, die die Engine bei jeder Abfrage selbst neu prüft.
de.stampSuffix: Die Endung der Tabelle der Verzeichnisstempel.
de.editSuffix: Die Endung des Änderungsindex, der jeden Eintrag den Zeilen zuordnet, die ihn nennen.
de.maximumRecordBytes: Die meisten Bytes eines Memo-Eintrags, die gelesen werden.
de.maximumPlanBytes: Die meisten Bytes eines geplanten Ausschnitts, die gelesen werden (256 MiB).
de.maximumRelevanceBytes: Die meisten Bytes einer Relevanztabelle, die gelesen werden (64 MiB).
de.maximumRecheckBytes: Die meisten Bytes einer Neupruef-Tabelle, die gelesen werden (256 MiB).
de.maximumStampBytes: Die meisten Bytes einer Stempeltabelle, die gelesen werden (64 MiB).
de.maximumEditBytes: Die meisten Bytes eines Änderungsindex, die gelesen werden (128 MiB).
de.maximumEditPaths: Die meisten geänderten Pfade, die eine Änderungsverfeinerung neu prüft, bevor sie stattdessen plant.
de.maximumEditRows: Die meisten Zeilen, die eine Änderungsverfeinerung neu prüft, bevor sie stattdessen plant.
de.maximumDerivedQuestions: Die meisten abgeleiteten Fakten, die das Memo in einem Kindprozess erneut fragt.
de.maximumRows: Die meisten Faktenzeilen, die ein versiegelter Ausschnitt halten darf.
de.leafSymlinkCheckConcurrency: Wie viele Blattpfade gleichzeitig auf symbolische Links geprüft werden.
de.environmentPrefixes: Die Präfixe der Umgebungsvariablen, die zum Memo-Schlüssel gehören.
de.argumentsDenied: Die Argumente, die nicht zum Memo-Schlüssel gehören.
de.stamped: Die Faktenarten, deren Verzeichnislisten durch Verzeichnisstempel verbürgt werden.
de.following: Die Faktenarten, die symbolischen Links folgen.
de.outputs: Die Verzeichnisse, in die ein Build seine eigenen Ergebnisse schreibt; ihre Listen werden bei jeder Abfrage neu geprüft.
de.environmentDenied: Die Umgebungsvariablen, die nie zum Memo-Schlüssel gehören.
de.relevance: Die geschlossene Tabelle dessen, was jede Faktenart liest.
de.carry: Welche generationsweiten Hashes gleich sein müssen, damit ein versiegelter Ausschnitt unter einer neueren Generation geliefert wird.
de.texts: Die englischen und deutschen Meldungen des Memos.
de.expect: Die Umgebungsvariable, die den Memo-Zustand trägt, den ein Planer-Kind vorfinden soll.
de.planOutput: Die Umgebungsvariable, die einem Planer-Kind sagt, wohin es den Plan des Graphen schreibt.
de.requestedAt: Die Umgebungsvariable, die den Zeitpunkt trägt, zu dem der Graph angefordert wurde.
de.pointerMaximumBytes: Die meisten Bytes einer Generations-Zeigerdatei, die gelesen werden (64 KiB).
de.deriveMaximumNames: Die meisten Namen, die eine Ableitungsanfrage oder -antwort aufführt.
de.deriveNameCharacters: Die meisten Zeichen eines Namens in einer Ableitungsanfrage oder -antwort.
de.abortCheckMask: Die Maske des Zeilenzählers: die Zeilenschleife prüft auf Abbruch, wenn der Zähler unter ihr null ist.
de.planFlushBytes: Die Größe, ab der der Plan-Schreiber seinen Puffer in die Datei schreibt (1 MiB).
de.planArrayChunkRows: Die Feldelemente, die der Plan-Schreiber auf einmal serialisiert.
